deep.reconstruction:
Context: folio 60r (previous page) is a draft of the introduction to Riemann's 1858 note 'Ein Beitrag zur Elektrodynamik', which he submitted to the Göttingen Society and then withdrew; it was published posthumously in 1867 in Poggendorff's Annalen. Its thesis is that the electrodynamic (and electromotive) actions of galvanic currents can be explained if the action of one electric mass on others propagates with a constant speed, equal to the speed of light within observational error. That page also states the working assumption that current intensities may be treated as constant during the propagation time from one conductor to the other.

This page (60v) is a fresh start of the same paper.

(1) Title: 'Neue Theorie der electrodynamischen Wirkungen galvanischer Ströme' (New theory of the electrodynamic actions of galvanic currents).

(2) A struck-out opening sentence: 'Über die Bewegung der positiven und negativen electrischen Theilchen mache ich die Voraussetzung, daß ...' (Concerning the motion of the positive and negative electric particles I make the assumption that ...). This is the Weber/Fechner two-fluid picture used in the published paper: each conductor element contains positive and negative particles e moving in opposite directions.

(3) A single formula: 'Es ist also ∫_0^t Σ e dτ = t ρ'. A second integral ∫_0^t ... is crossed out, and the right-hand symbol is uncertain (ρ, q or g).

Most plausible reading (mine, not certain): the sum Σ e runs over the electric particles in a fixed conductor element. The assumption about particle motion (constant currents, stationary distribution) implies this sum is independent of time and equals a constant ρ, the net charge, i.e. the density times the element. Hence the time integral from 0 to t is t·ρ. Alternatively the integrand may originally have carried a velocity factor, Σ e dx/dτ, giving t times a current component. That is the form used in the published paper, where Σ e ∂x/∂t is expressed through the current intensity i and ∂x/∂s.

The derivation breaks off here. No further computation is on the page. The next page (61) is unrelated algebra on quartic invariants and does not continue this text.
errors: No mathematical error can be identified; the page holds only a title, a cancelled sentence and one formula fragment.

The right-hand symbol of the formula is ambiguous in the image (ρ, q or g). The meaning of the identity depends on an assumption that was cancelled before it was stated, so the step is unjustified as it stands on the page.
If the intended integrand was Σ e (with no velocity factor), the identity is just the time integral of a constant. It is trivially correct given a stationary charge in each element.

results.what: Draft opening of the paper proposing that electric action propagates with finite (light) speed, i.e. retarded potentials, used to derive Weber-type electrodynamic forces between galvanic currents
results.modern_name: Retarded potential / finite-speed propagation of the electric potential (pre-Maxwellian electrodynamics)
results.usually_credited_to: B. Riemann (1858, published 1867); independently L. Lorenz (1867); Gauss's 1845 letter to Weber anticipates the idea

results.what: Time integral of the charge sum in a conductor element under stationary-current assumptions: ∫_0^t Σ e dτ = t·ρ
results.modern_name: Stationarity of charge density for steady currents (∂ρ/∂t = 0)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's well-known 1858 electrodynamics note, posthumously published in 1867 and long credited to him. The page adds only an alternative title and an abandoned opening, with no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: If Σe = ρ is constant in time, then ∫_0^t Σ e dτ = tρ (result 0).
Alternative reading: with Σ e dx/dτ = i ∂x/∂s (steady current), the time integral equals t·i·∂x/∂s.

transcription_corrections: The opening of the formula line reads 'Es ist also' (not a separate symbol).
The right-hand side '= tρ' is uncertain; the last letter could be ρ, q or g.
A second integral ∫_0^t ... is fully crossed out between the first integral and the equals sign; the machine rendering [-∫_0^t ...-] is right.
Title reading 'Neue Theorie der electrodynamischen Wirkungen galvanischer Ströme' is consistent with the image and with the previous page.
